Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for an individual to join our Data Center Engineering Operations Team. Responsible for asset and inventory management

jobs.title: Head of Validation and Systems Engineering
jobs.description:
Join the team bringing advanced autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

We are seeking a Head of Validation and Systems Engineering
to lead validation, verification, and systems engineering as an integrated discipline. In this role, you will define the criteria for every unsupervised deployment and serve as the technical authority on readiness, participating in critical launch decisions. You will develop a validation architecture where adding a new machine or capability is an incremental, evidence-based process. Rather than inheriting old frameworks, you will leverage cutting-edge research and create new best practices for an emerging industry.

Our machines already operate unsupervised at customer sites. Everything ahead—introducing more machine types, tackling new tasks each quarter, expanding to new sites—pushes the boundaries of the safety standards that have brought us this far.

What you will own

Safety validation of the system. Design the metrics, scenario libraries, and architectural coverage that quantify end-to-end behavioral safety — and make them hold up as the machine set and task set expand.
A validation architecture that generalizes. Decide what evidence is platform-independent and what must be re-established per machine, per task, per site. Turn the safety case into something composable instead of something rewritten.
Systems engineering. Own requirements decomposition and traceability from mission-level intent through subsystems, and use validation findings to expose the gaps, ambiguities, and conflicts that feed back into design.
V&V strategy and infrastructure. Choose the right instrument for each claim — log playback, closed-loop physics simulation, structured proving-ground testing, or on-site work — and specify the tooling and sim capability needed to make those instruments trustworthy across a growing fleet.
Hardware and functional safety. Validate the sensing, compute, and actuation kit we install on customer machines, including functional-safety readiness of safety-critical paths, as that kit is ported onto new platforms.
The org. Grow a team of software, systems, test, and hardware engineers plus data scientists, and scale it ahead of the machine count rather than behind it.
Decision-grade reporting. Define the KPIs — verification coverage, defect trends, release readiness, system maturity — and turn dense test data into the small number of charts that let leadership, customers, and insurers make a call.

What the first year looks like

A V&V framework and safety case structure that spans multiple machine types and an expanding task set, and that engineering, customers, and insurers all recognize as rigorous.
A scenario and coverage model built for the machines and tasks we have not shipped yet, not just the ones we have.
Readiness criteria that generalize — so the second platform, and the tenth, clear the bar faster than the first did without clearing a lower one.
A team that outlives any single launch.

Background

BS or advanced degree in engineering, physics, or another technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years in test planning and experimental design for safety-critical autonomous or robotic systems, with a bias toward safety and repeatability.
Track record building and leading multidisciplinary technical organizations — software, systems, hardware, test, and data science under one roof.
Depth in sensing and compute: cameras, lidar, radar, GNSS, IMUs, edge compute, embedded controllers.
Fluency in data analysis and test automation (Python, C/C++) sufficient to interrogate results yourself, not only to review them.
Experience running many parallel test activities across non-colocated teams, sites, and stakeholders.
Judgment about when a claim is proven and when it merely looks proven.

Ways to stand out

You have taken a driverless or unsupervised system through to real deployment and personally held the readiness gate — and then had to do it again for a second platform.
You have scaled a validation program across a heterogeneous fleet, multiple sites, or successive hardware generations.
You have authored or led a formal safety case, or contributed to safety standards work (UL 4600, ISO 26262, ISO 21448, or off-road equivalents).
Functional safety experience on vertically integrated or custom hardware.
Familiarity with heavy construction machines — excavators, articulated dump trucks, dozers, wheel loaders, motor graders.
A record of external technical contribution: publications, keynotes, standards bodies, or research leadership. We want this role visible in the field, and we will support that.

How we work

We are a startup, so we look for engineers with an appetite for agility. We do not compromise on safety and we still find ways to move extremely fast — the entire point of this role is that those two things are compatible when the evidence is good enough.

Our roles are often flexible. If you don't fit all the criteria, or are in another location (especially one where we have an office like SF or NY) please apply anyway! We'd love to consider you.

Description

The Director of Embedded Software Engineering will lead mission-critical embedded software development for Amazon Leo's satellite bus systems, ensuring our satellite constellation meets aggressive reliability, security, and performance targets from manufacturing through end-of-life operations.

This role owns all embedded software development and systems testing for satellite spacecraft systems — including flight software, real-time operating systems, avionics, and on-orbit software validation. You will architect the software that sits on the satellite, manage the end-to-end software stack to bring up the satellite, and lead comprehensive system testing to ensure spacecraft readiness for launch and on-orbit operations.

This is a highly technical leadership role requiring hands-on embedded software architecture expertise combined with the ability to build and scale high-performing engineering organizations. You will work in constrained hardware environments where computing resources (processing power, memory, power consumption) are severely limited. A satellite has 600+ unique processors — it's like having its own compact data center in space — requiring sophisticated embedded software solutions to coordinate this complexity.

Key job responsibilities

As a group leader, you will anticipate bottlenecks, provide escalation management, anticipate and make tradeoffs, and balance the business needs versus technical constraints. The ability to take large, complex projects and break them down into manageable pieces, develop functional specifications, then deliver them in a successful and timely manner is expected. Maturity, judgment, negotiation skills, ability to influence, analytical talent and leadership are essential to success in this role.

Embedded Software Architecture & Development

Define and implement end-to-end embedded software architecture for satellite bus systems
Lead development of real-time operating system (RTOS) implementations for spacecraft control, including scheduling algorithms and embedded design patterns
Architect Linux OS solutions for satellite systems
Drive hardware bring-up processes: boot, hardware verification, and comprehensive testing
Design and implement control systems, redundancy management, and health check software
Develop and oversee software for custom ASICs and FPGAs used in spacecraft systems
Architect solutions for complex application synchronization (e.g., global time clock syncing)
Address avionics systems challenges unique to spacecraft operations

Flight software and spacecraft control
Attitude determination and control systems (ADCS)
Power management and distribution
Thermal control systems
Command and data handling
Fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR)
Onboard autonomy and health monitoring

Establish multi-test environments and continuous test/deployment pipelines
Drive software quality from prototype satellites to production at scale

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

Provide close partnership with Hardware Engineering teams throughout the development lifecycle — from component design through integration and launch
Create documentation for worldwide regulatory bodies
Work closely with research teams to evaluate and simulate system-level performance
Provide technical leadership while meeting aggressive project schedules
Drive operational excellence and optimize system performance (e.g., battery usage, resource management)

Team Building & Organizational Leadership

Scale the embedded software engineering organization from current state to production needs
Hire and develop exceptional embedded software engineers and leaders
Manage multiple engineering teams as a leader of leaders (100+ people)
Foster a culture of innovation, speed, and technical excellence consistent with a "new space" mindset
Develop talent pipeline for specialized embedded systems expertise

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related STEM discipline
US Citizenship, Permanent Resident (Green Card), or Political Asylum status required
Min 10+ years of experience as a manager of managers leading multiple engineering teams
Proven track record building and scaling engineering organizations (70+ people)
Demonstrated ability to grow teams from scratch and scale to production operations
Experience managing directors, principal engineers, and senior technical leaders

Technical Experience

Min 10+ years of embedded software design and development for mission-critical systems
Hands-on experience with embedded software architecture and implementation — must be comfortable conducting architectural reviews and discussing technical implementations directly with engineers
Strong Unix/Linux and systems development skills
Proven experience with real-time operating systems (RTOS) architecture and implementation
Deep understanding of embedded software design patterns and best practices
Experience with hardware-software integration in constrained environments
Track record taking projects from scoping requirements to successful launch

Software Development Methodology

"Build quickly" mindset — test on the ground and anticipate how it will work in space
Proven ability to balance speed with reliability in aerospace-grade environments
Experience with rapid iteration and continuous test/deployment pipelines

Preferred Qualifications

Aerospace & Satellite Systems Experience

Hands-on experience with aerospace and avionics systems and techniques for high reliability/robust design
Experience leading satellite bus software development — flight software, attitude control, power management, spacecraft systems
On-orbit software testing and validation experience for operational satellites ("testing SW on satellites")

Experience working on subsystems and subcomponents (not just system integration)

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Job Description

AECOM Information Technology is seeking a Director, Enterprise ServiceNow Platform, to lead, own, and evolve our global ServiceNow ecosystem that supports enterprise workflow automation, digital operations, and employee services at scale.

This leader will serve as the global platform owner for ServiceNow, responsible for platform strategy, governance, roadmap execution, demand management, and continuous improvement. This role is focused on advancing ServiceNow as a strategic enterprise capability, not simply managing operational support or teams that use the tool.

The ideal candidate has experience owning a large-scale ServiceNow environment, partnering with business leaders, leading delivery teams and vendors, and creating scalable solutions that improve automation, user experience, and business outcomes.

This position will offer flexibility for hybrid work schedules to include both in-office presence and telecommute/virtual work, to be based from either Houston or Dallas, TX.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Platform Ownership & Strategy

Own the global ServiceNow platform roadmap, governance model, standards, and long-term maturity strategy, and continuously evolve the ServiceNow operating model to ensure scalable governance, delivery consistency, and operational transparency.
Define how ServiceNow capabilities are prioritized, delivered, adopted, and continuously improved across the enterprise.
Partner with IT, HR, Finance, Security, Operations, and other business groups to translate business needs into scalable platform solutions and facilitate governance forums that align priorities and proactively manage risk.

Governance, Delivery & Continuous Improvement

Lead the ServiceNow demand intake process, backlog prioritization, enhancement delivery, release planning, and platform lifecycle management, ensuring predictable delivery outcomes through disciplined Agile planning, capacity management, and execution, with accountability for enforcing governance standards and intake discipline.
Establish scalable processes around development standards, SDLC practices, integrations, upgrades, and platform health, ensuring only approved and prioritized work enters execution pipelines.
Drive adoption of ServiceNow best practices to maximize out-of-the-box capabilities while reducing unnecessary customization and technical debt.

Team & Partner Leadership

Lead and develop ServiceNow platform teams, including internal resources and external implementation/MSP partners.
Manage vendor accountability across delivery quality, timelines, technical standards, business outcomes, and predictable execution.
Build a culture focused on ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Automation & Innovation

Identify opportunities to expand ServiceNow capabilities through workflow automation, self-service, AI, and improved user experiences.
Lead initiatives leveraging modern ServiceNow capabilities, including Now Assist, AI-enabled workflows, and enterprise automation.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree plus at least 12 years of ServiceNow experience, including 4 years of leadership experience, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Experience owning, managing, or leading ServiceNow platforms within large, complex enterprise environments.
Experience driving ServiceNow platform strategy, governance, roadmap planning, demand intake, backlog prioritization, and delivery execution to support enterprise business needs.
Experience partnering with business stakeholders, technology teams, and external vendors/MSPs to deliver scalable ServiceNow solutions, enhancements, integrations, and platform improvements.
Experience across ServiceNow capabilities such as ITSM, ITOM, ITAM, HRSD, CSM, SPM, CMDB, Knowledge Management, Employee Center, or Service Portals.
Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to influence technical teams, business partners, and senior stakeholders.
Due to the nature of this position, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of leadership experience managing ServiceNow platform, enterprise application, or digital workflow teams.
Experience leading ServiceNow transformation, modernization, or platform maturity initiatives.
ServiceNow certifications such as CSA, CAD, CTA, or CMA.
Agile certifications such as CSM, CSPO, SAFe, or equivalent experience.
Experience with ServiceNow AI capabilities, Now Assist, MoveWorks, automation, or workflow optimization.
Background in enterprise applications, platform engineering, software delivery, or solution architecture.
Experience working within large global or matrixed organizations.

Additional Information

Relocation assistance is not available for this position
Sponsorship for US work authorization is not available for this position, now or in the future.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $170000 to $220000.

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO)

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. We enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted SaaS provider. We create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact

Cyber defense doesn't scale through headcount alone. It scales when systems make defenders exponentially more effective. We're looking for a Sr Software Engineering Manager to join Cyber Defense Engineering and build the Applied AI Engineering function: a small, high-caliber engineering team applying AI and automation to some of the most challenging problems in cyber defense, protecting a platform trusted by thousands of the world's largest enterprises.

You'll own the architecture for systems that automate security incident investigations, accelerate threat hunting, operationalize threat intelligence, scale attack path management, and turn security issue management into measurable risk reduction. You'll also build the internal capability for security practitioners to extend that automation themselves, so your systems compound impact rather than create new bottlenecks.

This is a rare opportunity to define how AI transforms cyber defense at scale, with the technical latitude and executive backing to do it right.

What You'll Do

Own AI-Powered Security Architecture: Set the technical strategy and architecture for AI-powered use cases across cyber defense domains, including threat intelligence, threat hunting, security operations, incident response, attack path management, and security issue management
Unify Data Into Defender-Ready Systems: Build solutions that fully leverage internal telemetry, asset data, context, and external intelligence to deliver domain-specific use cases that enable cyber defenders
Enable Practitioner Self-Sufficiency: Empower security practitioners to extend and maintain automation themselves, compounding your team's impact over time
Build a World-Class Engineering Team: Recruit and grow a high-performing engineering team, setting a high technical bar and building durable career paths
Drive Shipping Velocity: Establish a rapid, low-risk shipping cadence, owning architecture decisions and removing blockers so your team moves fast without breaking things
Shape the Roadmap Cross-Functionally: Partner closely with Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Hunting, Red Team, and more on priorities

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry.
10 to 15 years building and shipping software systems at scale (backend, full stack, data, or platform engineering) OR similar experience with education
Proven track record of building or scaling a high-performing engineering team, with 2+ years managing engineers
Deep technical fluency: you can code review, evaluate architecture tradeoffs, and unblock the hardest problems your team faces
Demonstrated ability to distinguish "build it ourselves" from "enable someone else to build it": this role demands both engineering execution and a coaching mindset
Comfort operating with significant ambiguity, standing up a new function from the ground up
A track record of establishing engineering best practices and holding a team to a high bar of technical excellence

Preferred Qualifications

Security domain experience (incident response, SOC, threat intelligence, hunting, vulnerability management, etc.), or a strong appetite to learn it quickly
Experience applying AI/ML to operational or workflow automation at scale
Familiarity with modern data infrastructure
Experience building enablement programs, internal platforms, or tooling for non-engineer end users

, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Develop and implement a comprehensive systems strategy aligned with the university's goals and objectives.
Provide strategic direction for systems operations and administration, storage, cloud computing and virtualization, application system and security support, and Campus Safety Services.
Collaborate with the Assistant CTO and other senior leaders to prioritize systems initiatives and align them with institutional priorities.
Develop staff, set clear performance expectations, and manage workload and operational tasks across the systems team.
Work with other groups within IT and other business units as needed to develop solutions for unique system requirements, including technical and regulatory requirements.

Lead the evaluation, selection, and adoption of new platform technologies to enhance systems capabilities.
Ensure new implementations are documented, supportable, and aligned with institutional standards and architecture.

Ensure that all documentation and databases are up to date and accurate, including asset inventory and configuration records.

DevOps, Automation, and Process Improvement

Manage the DevOps resource supporting the infrastructure organization, receiving strategic DevOps and automation requirements from the Assistant CTO and directing the work accordingly.
Identify commonly performed actions, repeated requests, and recurring requirements across every area reporting to this role, including systems operations, storage, virtualization, cloud, application system support, and Campus Safety Services.
Define, document, and standardize the processes behind that work so it can be measured and performed consistently by both full-time employees and the managed service provider.
Identify and prioritize the automation opportunities with the greatest return on team efficiency, and direct their design, build, and adoption.
Measure the effect of automation and process improvement on toil, cycle time, and error rates, and adjust priorities based on results.
Promote the adoption of automation and consistent operating practice across the teams reporting to this role.

Application System and Security Support

Own the systems and middleware layer beneath the university's enterprise and departmental applications, including database platforms, web services, and load balancing.
Ensure that these platforms are appropriately sized, patched, monitored, hardened, and recoverable.
Partner with application owners and the Office of Information Security to remediate vulnerabilities and apply security controls at the system and middleware layer.
Coordinate maintenance windows and upgrade planning with application stakeholders to minimize disruption to academic and administrative operations.

Oversee the technology, operation, and support of campus safety systems, including physical card access, video surveillance, emergency radios, and the emergency phone system.
Ensure the security, reliability, and availability of these physical security and life-safety systems.
Oversee deployment, upgrade, and lifecycle planning for campus safety technology, including coverage associated with building renovation and construction projects.
Collaborate with Campus Police, Facilities, and external vendors and integrators to align technology capability with campus safety requirements.

Security, Compliance, and Resilience

Ensure all systems components meet institutional security and compliance requirements, and implement best practices for securing server, storage, virtualization, cloud, and campus safety infrastructure.
Ensure system designs and procedures are aligned with, and capable of enforcing, university policies and best practices.
Ensure backup, recovery, and business continuity capabilities are designed, documented, and regularly tested against defined recovery objectives.
Ensure vulnerabilities are remediated within institutional service level targets and provide the Information Security operations team with the access and tooling required to identify, locate, and isolate systems involved in security incidents.
Support audit activity and the production of control evidence, and assist Information Security in drafting policies that overlap with the systems team.

Budget, Vendor, and Resource Management

Develop and manage the operating and capital budget for the systems team and Campus Safety Services technology.
Ensure efficient use of resources and identify opportunities for cost savings and license optimization.
Oversee vendor relationships and negotiate contracts for systems, storage, cloud, and campus safety related services and products, interacting directly with vendors, resellers, and integrators.
Plan and forecast refresh and renewal cycles to support multi-year budget development.

Performs all other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor.

Qualifications

4-year bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or Information Technology, or equivalent experience. A bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field is preferred.
Minimum of 7 years of experience, including direct leadership of a systems, infrastructure, or operations team.
Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to develop and retain technical staff.
Excellent strategic thinking and planning abilities.
Deep understanding of server, storage, virtualization, and cloud computing technologies across both Windows and Linux environments.
Working knowledge of the middleware layer supporting enterprise applications, including database platforms, web services, and load balancing.
Ability to direct DevOps and automation resources against strategic requirements set by the Assistant CTO.
Knowledge of physical access control, video surveillance, and emergency communications systems.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to serve as a senior escalation point during major incidents.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Experience developing and managing operating and capital budgets and negotiating with vendors.

Preferred Certifications: Certifications are preferred, not required, and no candidate is expected to hold all of them. Credentials relevant to WPI's technology stack include:

Windows Server: Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Administrator Associate (Exam AZ-802), or the predecessor Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate (Exams AZ-800 and AZ-801).
Cloud platforms: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305); AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate or AWS Certified Solutions Architect.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO)

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. We enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted SaaS provider. We create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact

Cyber defense doesn't scale through headcount alone. It scales when systems make defenders exponentially more effective. We're looking for a Sr Software Engineering Manager to join Cyber Defense Engineering and build the Applied AI Engineering function: a small, high-caliber engineering team applying AI and automation to some of the most challenging problems in cyber defense, protecting a platform trusted by thousands of the world's largest enterprises.

You'll own the architecture for systems that automate security incident investigations, accelerate threat hunting, operationalize threat intelligence, scale attack path management, and turn security issue management into measurable risk reduction. You'll also build the internal capability for security practitioners to extend that automation themselves, so your systems compound impact rather than create new bottlenecks.

This is a rare opportunity to define how AI transforms cyber defense at scale, with the technical latitude and executive backing to do it right.

What You'll Do

Own AI-Powered Security Architecture: Set the technical strategy and architecture for AI-powered use cases across cyber defense domains, including threat intelligence, threat hunting, security operations, incident response, attack path management, and security issue management
Unify Data Into Defender-Ready Systems: Build solutions that fully leverage internal telemetry, asset data, context, and external intelligence to deliver domain-specific use cases that enable cyber defenders

Build a World-Class Engineering Team: Recruit and grow a high-performing engineering team, setting a high technical bar and building durable career paths

10 to 15 years building and shipping software systems at scale (backend, full stack, data, or platform engineering) OR similar experience with education

Comfort operating with significant ambiguity, standing up a new function from the ground up

Security domain experience (incident response, SOC, threat intelligence, hunting, vulnerability management, etc.), or a strong appetite to learn it quickly
Experience applying AI/ML to operational or workflow automation at scale
Familiarity with modern data infrastructure
Experience building enablement programs, internal platforms, or tooling for non-engineer end users

Your job is to show them how they get there: architect the systems, mentor your team to build working proof-of-concepts and get marketing leaders excited about what's possible.

Personalization & Platform Strategy

Provide expert guidance on emerging tools and technology trends, and act as the technical translator between what the business wants and what is achievable.

Own the department's technology architecture roadmap, working directly with business leaders to translate multi-year vision into deliverable increments.
